scenarios.title: A document link is not document access
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you explain the access blocker and ask for what you need, without accepting blame or promising an unagreed review deadline?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The shared location and reported password prompt are documented. Priya independently reports the prompt; no message supplies a password. Missing proof of delivery is not proof that a password was never sent elsewhere.

scenarios.title: The deadline moved a day earlier
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you respond to the earlier deadline and explain any trade-off or clarification you need?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: Alex originally set Thursday 19 November at 15:00 and now asks for Wednesday at 16:00. History supports the change, not a promise that Sam can meet it.

scenarios.title: Two urgent tasks and one person
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you ask for a clear priority while giving a factual update on the support queue and slide request?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The original instruction puts support first until fewer than 10 tickets remain; the recorded count is still 22 when slides are requested. No later message resolves the priority conflict.

scenarios.title: A workshop conflicts with approved time away
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you flag the workshop clash and help arrange coverage without implying that you are available during approved time away?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: Alex explicitly approved Wednesday after 14:00 and Jordan confirms cover. The new workshop is at 14:30 on that same day.

scenarios.title: A last-minute Saturday request
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you answer based on your own availability and ask what arrangements are needed before anyone commits you?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The published rota is Monday-Friday and no weekend cover has been booked. The history does not establish whether Sam is personally available on Saturday or whether extra work is compensated.

scenarios.title: Clarifying who built the dashboard
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you correct the ownership description respectfully while recognising Priya's review contribution?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: Sam describes implementing the calculation and drill-down; Priya independently confirms that she reviewed those and changed labels/colours. Do not turn a credit correction into a claim about anyone's motives.

scenarios.title: A receipt is attached but finance is still waiting
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you point Alex to the receipt and distinguish submitting it from approval or reimbursement?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The tracker entry and receipt location are recorded and Jordan confirms the link and amount. Finance approval and payment have not been confirmed.

scenarios.title: More professional, but in what way?
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you ask for a concrete example or criterion while keeping the revision moving?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The three-part format is documented, but the later feedback does not identify what wording is unsuitable or what polish means. History cannot establish Alex's hidden expectations or feelings.

scenarios.title: A handover is blocked by an external feed
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you explain the dependency, identify the next action and avoid promising a delivery time you do not control?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: Morgan owns the vendor contact, the corrected feed missed noon and Sam cannot run final checks without it. The vendor's revised 16:00 estimate is not proof of delivery.

scenarios.title: 142 and 156 can both describe the same extract
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you explain the difference between gross and net orders and clarify which number belongs in the report?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The extract has 156 gross orders minus 8 cancellations and 6 refunds, giving 142 net. Jordan explicitly requests the net number for the board report; no arithmetic error is established.

scenarios.title: CSV was agreed; PDF is now requested too
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you explain the scope change and ask for a decision on time, scope or resources before committing?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The recorded release scope is CSV only; Morgan says PDF has not been promised. Passing CSV tests does not establish that PDF can be added in the same slot or budget.

scenarios.title: A missed meeting with an earlier acknowledgement
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you respond after missing the review? Try checking a claim that nobody told you about it against the saved conversation.
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: The assertion that Sam was never told about the Friday 11:00 review is contradicted by Alex's invitation and Sam's explicit acknowledgement. The history does not say why Sam missed it, so no excuse or admission should be invented.

scenarios.title: A remembered conversation is not written approval
scenarios.writingPrompt: How would you describe your recollection and request clear confirmation before booking the course?
scenarios.evidenceExpectation: Sam recalls a kitchen conversation but has no written approval and has not booked. Jordan's policy is not evidence of what Alex said. Whether Alex approved the spend verbally remains unverified.
